archetype.name: Pocket Passer (precision timing)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower from shotgun who wins with accuracy and anticipation between the hashes and outside the numbers, and who barely uses his legs.

report.headline: The most accurate passer in football, running a pass-first offense at its peak
report.take:
Burrow is what he has been at his best: a shotgun timing passer who wins from the pocket with accuracy rather than arm talent or legs. His 10.21 CPOE leads all 54 qualifiers. He has led the league in that stat before (2021) and finished third in 2024, so the accuracy is his identity, not a fluke. What has changed is how much the offense leans on it. Cincinnati passes 10.6 points more often than situation predicts, the most in the league, and he is turning that volume into a league-best 310.6 yards and 3 touchdowns a game.

The engine is the 10-to-19-yard window. On 75 intermediate attempts he is at 0.833 EPA a play with a 76% success rate and a 21.2 CPOE. Everything thrown 10+ air yards has added 99.2 EPA, more than his entire dropback total of 97, because the short game and especially the screen game give points back. Tee Higgins (0.698 EPA per target) and Ja'Marr Chase (0.55) are the two best targets any quarterback has. Oddly, Burrow is also a little less aggressive than last year: tight-window throws are down 4.7 points. He is throwing into open spots and hitting them.

The numbers hide two things. First, the season has two halves. In September he was ordinary: -1.9 EPA against Tampa's second-ranked defense and five sacks at Houston. Over the five-game win streak since, he is at 0.418 EPA a dropback, and that run came mostly against defenses ranked 18th or worse. Second, some of this efficiency sits above even his own ceiling. A CPOE near double digits, 20 red-zone touchdowns on 53 attempts and a 7.9% touchdown rate are not numbers a passer holds for 17 games.

The interceptions also have not gone away. He has thrown 6, ranked 38th, including three in the Tennessee shootout, and his career turnover ranks have always lagged his efficiency. Expect him to stay a top-five producer with a league-leading volume floor, but cooling from the 34-point pace of the last three weeks back toward the low-to-mid 20s.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy carries the offense
strengths.body: His 10-to-19-yard throws are the most productive area of his game: 0.833 EPA per attempt with a 21.2 CPOE. Timing on outs, digs and back-shoulder throws to two receivers who win outside produces that. The skill is real and repeatable, but a CPOE that high on 75 attempts will drift down even if he stays very good there.

strengths.title: League-leading accuracy, backed by career
strengths.body: A 10.21 CPOE ranks first. He has posted top-three CPOE seasons in 2021 and 2024, so this is his baseline skill rather than one hot stretch. His bad-throw rate has risen from last year's league-best 5%, yet it still ranks third. The accuracy floor is safe even as the peak cools.

strengths.title: Pressure no longer becomes sacks
strengths.body: Only 19.7% of his pressures have turned into sacks, ninth-best. His career rates ran from roughly 29% to 37%, often near the bottom of the league. His time to throw is unchanged, so the gain reads as quicker decisions under duress rather than a better line; the team's hit rate allowed ranks only 19th. That partly holds, but it is the stat most exposed if a starting guard misses time.

concerns.title: Efficiency above his own ceiling
concerns.body: His completion rate over expected is well above his best previous season, and 20 of his 27 touchdowns have come on 53 red-zone throws. A 7.9% touchdown rate, and 10.9% over the last five, is a pace no passer holds. Some of it is the offense's design and two great receivers. Some of it is a hot streak against Tennessee, Miami and Atlanta that will cool.

concerns.title: The interception tax remains
concerns.body: Six interceptions rank 38th even in a historically efficient season. Five came on throws to the right, and three came in one game against Tennessee. This fits his career: his 2021 and 2022 seasons ranked near the bottom in interceptions despite top-10 efficiency. It is the cost of a volume passer hunting intermediate windows, and it will keep producing the occasional ugly game.

concerns.title: No support from the short game
concerns.body: Throws behind the line have cost 12.7 EPA, and Chase Brown's 54 targets are a net negative. Under-center dropbacks are below average, and the rushing offense ranks 14th. Burrow is carrying an offense with no easy-button plays. That is why the pass rate is so high, and why a bad accuracy day has little behind it to cushion the result.

trend.note: He opened with two flat games, -1.9 and -0.1 EPA, then climbed to a 5-0 run at 0.418 EPA per dropback. Weeks 8-10 were the best of the year at 380.7 yards and 4 touchdowns a game, capped by 21.4 EPA against Pittsburgh.

nextGame.headline: A soft, pass-funnel Washington defense meets a peaking passer
nextGame.body:
Washington is a good matchup for what Burrow does. Its defense ranks 22nd in pass EPA and 27th in sack rate, and it has allowed 280.4 passing yards a game, 30th. Offenses pass on it 4.6 points more than normal, the third-strongest pass funnel. Its best work is underneath, where it ranks 8th in short-pass EPA. That matters less for a passer who gets his value at 10+ air yards. Lead receivers and tight ends have both beaten their usual output against it. The Book makes Cincinnati a 6.5-point favorite with a 52.5 total, which points to a high-volume game script rather than an early lead that ends the passing.

Burrow is active and the QB1; the questionable tag on his record is a stale Week 2 entry. The availability that matters is guard Dalton Risner, a 94%-snap starter who left the Pittsburgh game with a knee injury and is questionable. A backup guard against a weak pass rush is manageable, but it is the one threat to his low sack rate. Andrei Iosivas being on IR costs little, since he played only two games. Washington's injuries are on its offense: Laremy Tunsil is on IR and guard Lucas Patrick is out. That leaves an 18th-ranked attack less likely to turn this into a track meet than the total implies.

keyMatchups.title: Chase against a leaky WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: Washington ranks 29th at holding lead receivers to their averages; WR1s score 4.5 PPR points over their norm against it. Chase has the most targets on the team, and Higgins has been even more efficient per target. Expect intermediate volume to both.

keyMatchups.title: Gesicki against the worst TE defense
keyMatchups.body: No defense has given lead tight ends more over their averages than Washington. Gesicki has been efficient on modest volume at 0.609 EPA per target. He is the easiest place for the extra touchdown to come from.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush versus a patched guard
keyMatchups.body: Washington's 27th-ranked sack rate and 24th-ranked hit rate give him clean pockets even if Risner sits. His worst game came when pressure got home, with five sacks at Houston. That only becomes a risk here if the interior replacement struggles badly.

nextGame.watch: Whether Risner plays, and if not, whether Washington can generate interior pressure that its sack rate says it rarely does.

restOfSeason.body:
The volume is structural. A league-high pass rate, two receivers among the most efficient in the sport and a run game that can't carry drives keep him near 37-40 attempts a week. Expect him to stay near the top of the league in yards. What should regress is the touchdown rate and the CPOE. A red zone converting at this clip and accuracy above his best previous seasons will both cool, so the 3-4 touchdown weeks become 2-3. The interceptions should continue at their usual rate, a bit under one a game.

I'd project 275-325 passing yards a game, 2.1-2.8 touchdowns and 0.5-0.9 interceptions, good for roughly 21-27 PPR points. That is still a top-five quarterback line, just below the 34-point peak of the last three weeks. The biggest risks are health on the interior line and tougher defenses: his two worst games came against Tampa's second-ranked unit and a Houston pass rush that got home.
swingFactors: Interior line holding up with Risner hurt
How far red-zone TD rate regresses

confidence.note: The profile is clear over 9 starts with a matching career history; the open question is how much of the extreme efficiency cools.
